Model C: freight-cost movement forecasts

Four algorithms and a no-change baseline. Direct H3/H6/H12 forecasts describe changes in the BLS freight index; values shown are index points.

Selected from validation

H3Gradient Boosting quantilesBest ML candidate: Gradient Boosting quantiles
H6No-change baselineBest ML candidate: Ridge + residual quantiles
H12Gradient Boosting quantilesBest ML candidate: Gradient Boosting quantiles

Selections use 2015-2019 validation and its pre-2020 known outcomes. H12 does not determine model selection. A baseline selection means no ML candidate met both validation coverage and MIS requirements.

Data and evaluation

Initial history: 2005-2014. Expanding annual validation fits: 2015-2019. Monthly disruption fits: 2020-2021 reference months. Later monitoring: 2022 onward. Every fit uses only targets assumed available then; the latest 24 eligible outcomes calibrate intervals and are held out from fitting the estimator.

Research evaluation using assumed publication dates and current historical snapshots. Historical release dates and original revision vintages remain unverified. The required FBX 2020-2021 comparison is still missing. Reference-month tests and the separate specification issue-date tests are saved with explicit labels.

What the results show

The validation-selected H3 model, Gradient Boosting quantiles, achieves 87.5% disruption coverage with MIS 0.845 times the baseline. Its test acceptance is reported independently of its validation selection.

Random Forest is the strongest H3 test candidate: 95.8% coverage, MIS ratio 0.683, and passes the recorded recovery gate. It was not selected by validation, so the test outcome does not replace the frozen recommendation.

At H6, the highest ML test coverage is 75.0%, below the required 90%. No candidate meets the H6 coverage requirement. These results support further research rather than a production acceptance claim.

Evaluation metrics

Coverage should be at least 90%. MIS ratio below 1 means better than the equally calibrated no-change baseline. Missing forecasts count as misses. MAPE measures median index error, while pinball and MIS evaluate the forecast distribution.

Interval-score comparison

Feature influence

These graphs describe the final fitted models. Ridge uses absolute standardized coefficients, expressed as shares of their total magnitude. Forest models use tree impurity importance; Gradient Boosting shows its P50 estimator only. These measures do not establish causation or forecast accuracy, and correlated features can share influence. The no-change baseline has no learned feature importance.

Training and validation loss

These are uncalibrated mean pinball-loss diagnostics on an initial chronological fit and a fixed 2015-2017 validation window. They do not use the disruption test. Ridge is plotted against training-set size, forests against tree count and Gradient Boosting against actual boosting stages. In-sample loss is diagnostic, not acceptance evidence.

Recovery of completed-outcome coverage

Each point uses the latest six forecasts whose outcomes are assumed published by that date. Recovery credit requires all six target months to be January 2020 or later. With six observations, the 90% threshold requires six of six inside the interval.

Latest forecasts

Based on the last supplied observation, August 2026. Its prototype issue date is September 2026. Targets are measured from that reference observation; these are freight-index movements, not route-specific charges in GBP.
